correctness.rationale: Independently checked RESULT.md lines 5–66, the two frozen verification programs, and ran the independently written standard-library script /workspace/branches/reproduce_square_ice.py. It selects two outgoing neighbors per vertex and enforces complementary choices on each shared edge when its second endpoint is visited. Thus every accepted assignment is an ice orientation, and each such orientation appears once. The coordinate construction checks all directed incidences belong to exactly one square; the enumeration returned 1 empty set with coefficient 144, six singletons each 24, all 15 pairs each 8, eight triples each 16 (all opposite-pair transversals), and the full set with coefficient 64. Reversal on a directed square preserves vertex balances and alters no edge of another square. Each component is therefore a free orbit of the commuting flips, exactly Q_d, with per-set multiplicity obtained by division by 2^d. Replay returned 600 states, 576 edges, the histogram {0:144,1:72,2:30,3:16,6:1}, and the exact isotropic spectrum including 224 zero eigenvalues. For any positive couplings tensor flip eigenvectors give the stated signed sums on each cube and RK eigenvalues given by twice subset sums. Only one six-cube realizes the kinetic minimum; every smaller cube omits at least three faces, so it cannot supply the first excitation. The full cube supplies the kinetic and RK gaps 2 min_i t_i; the RK zero count is one per cube, including isolated vertices.
